message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that would take several years to complete. Here’s why:

| Factor | Why it matters | Rough estimate |
|--------|----------------|----------------|
| **Height & Surface Area** | The tower is ~330 m tall and has a complex lattice structure with ~18 000 square meters of metal surface. | 18 000 m² |
| **Safety & Logistics** | Workers must be suspended at great heights, requiring extensive rigging, safety harnesses, and coordination with the Paris fire department. | 1–2 weeks per “painting shift” |
| **Weather Constraints** | Paint can only be applied under certain temperature and humidity conditions; rain or extreme heat can delay work. | 60–70 % of the year usable |
| **Paint & Equipment** | High‑altitude spray guns, protective coatings, and a dedicated crew of ~30–40 painters are needed. | 3–4 months of continuous work per season |
| **Regulatory & Heritage Restrictions** | The tower is a protected monument; any work must preserve its historic integrity, limiting the speed of application. | 1–2 months of planning per season |

**Putting it together**

- **Seasonal Work Window**: Roughly 8–9 months per year (the rest of the year is either too hot, too cold, or rainy).
- **Continuous Work Time**: About 3–4 months of nonstop painting per season.
- **Total Seasons Needed**: 2–3 seasons.

So, **painting the Eiffel Tower would likely take around 2–3 years** if you’re doing it in a single, continuous project. If you’re doing it in phases or as part of routine maintenance, it could be spread out over a longer period.
